title: HIRAKU contract
description: Shapes shared by every part of HIRAKU: the requirements file, the design, load cases, predictions, analyses, comparisons, causes, verdicts, judgements, tools, the project file and the events.jsonl line. Validate with hiraku.contract.validate(kind, obj), where kind is a key of $defs.

unit.description: Unit strings. A comparison is only made between equal unit strings; convert before comparing.

domain.description: Seven analysis domains plus assembly. Japanese names: handling 操安, powertrain 動力, aero 空力, crash 衝突, strength 強度信頼性, nvh 音振, thermal 熱, assembly 組み立て.

agent_id.description: lead = まとめ役, designer = 設計役, packager = パッケージ役, cae.<domain> = 分野ごとの CAE 役, system = HIRAKU itself (hooks, store), user = the person. designer.<module> = モジュールごとの設計役 (designs with modules).

base.description: Solver base. K0 hand calculation, K1 3D beam FE, K2 3D vehicle physics, K3 power and thermal circuit, K4 geometry, interference and people, K5 contribution and sensitivity.

test_id.description: Catalog test id, e.g. S1, P1, R1, R4.

flags.description: Product property flags (catalog section 1). ride 乗, lean 預, self_propelled 走, outdoor 外, rough 悪, public_road 公, battery 池, electric 電, pinch 挟, cargo 荷, standing 置, near_people 近, liquid 液, vibration 振, continuous 続, assembly 組, preload 張, sound 音, handheld 持. The speed range 速 is speed_class.

speed_class.description: 速: static 静, walk 歩 (<= 2 m/s), vehicle 車 (<= 40 km/h).

basis.description: Where the value comes from (citation or 'assumption').

requirements_file.description: Input file given to HIRAKU (YAML or JSON). In the MVP the design is fixed and named by design_file.

want.description: What the person wants to make, in their words.

default_loading.description: Who and what is on board when a load case does not say (params.loading). Omitted: two_cargo, the vehicle default. A one-person product (a care bed) says driver: one occupant, no cargo.

tests.description: Optional: run only these tests. When absent, tests are chosen from the catalog by flags.

design_file.description: Optional: path (relative to the repository) of a fixed design JSON.

beyond.description: Tests that also get a load case beyond their limit (id ending -beyond, title starting 限界の外), for showing the failing side.

stop_after.description: A run that ends on purpose after an early step. picks: after domains.picked and the hearing (records for picking domains only; no design is made). The run ends done, with the reason saying so.

hearing.description: Who settles the missing requirement items. code (missing = code): start_run fills them from the file and defaults before the agents start. claude: start_run leaves them open and the lead asks the person with ask_user (wait_seconds). Copied to the project when the run starts.

dims_mm.description: e.g. rect_tube: {b, h, t}; round_tube: {d, t}.

verified.description: false until the value is checked against the cited source.

stress_strain.description: Engineering stress-strain points [strain, stress MPa] from 0 to the tensile strength; at least yield and tensile.

fatigue.description: S-N data: the parent material and named weld details (IIW FAT classes).

sources.description: Per field name: the source (title, table, URL) and whether it was checked.

support.description: Something that touches the ground: a wheel, caster or leg. K2 builds the vehicle from this list.

kc_table.description: Path of a K&C table file.

bushings.description: Compliance of the arms' inner bushings and the tie rod (the C of K&C). Missing values are assumed by the solver and written to the analysis assumptions.

hardpoints_mm.description: Suspension pickup points of this support in design coordinates (mm), written by the code that builds the design (the K2 team's hardpoint keys, e.g. upper and lower arm inner pivots, tie rod inner point, damper_upper, damper_lower). The solvers and the screen read them from here, so there is one source.

frame_node.description: Frame node that carries this support's load into the frame.

tire.description: Tyre model of this support. Without it the K2 team's default tyre file is used.

coefficients.description: Path (relative to the repository) of a tyre coefficient file in data/tyres/.

kind.description: frame, suspension, wheel, battery, motor, controller, seat, occupant, cargo, body, rollbar, ... Occupants and cargo are parts (kind occupant / cargo); a load case chooses which are on board with params.loading.

rpy_deg.description: Roll, pitch, yaw of the box.

carried_by.description: Frame nodes that carry this part's weight (split equally unless the solver says otherwise).

system.description: The functional system the part belongs to, e.g. drive, steering, brake, suspension, seat, restraint, rops, lighting, battery, control, body, cargo. Written by the code that builds the design.

to.description: A part id, member id, frame node id (an id in nodes, where a part is fixed at a joint of the frame), support id or '<support>.<hardpoint>'.

via.description: How it is joined or what passes: bolt, weld, spline, ball_joint, pin, bushing, rest, wire, hose, ...

carries.description: What goes through the link: torque, steer, brake, load, power, signal.

at_mm.description: Where the two are joined: a point on both shapes (the generator computes it; H1-joints checks it lies on both within 2 mm).

axis.description: For a pin, bushing, hinge or ball joint: the direction of its axis (unit vector), so the joint can be drawn and turned about it.

connects_to.description: What this part is joined to, so code can follow a chain end to end (motor to driven wheels, steering wheel to knuckles).

material.description: Key into design.materials (as for members): what the part is made of, for its mass, strength and look.

finish.description: Surface of the part as made (for the look and for corrosion notes); missing: as its material comes.

joint.description: How the members meeting at this node are joined. Absent: not stated (the ladder_4w generator's frame nodes are welded).

part.description: Part id this member belongs to.

name.description: The member's name for a person (Japanese), e.g. 左のレール (前の車軸から足元まで); written by the generator, shown by the screen.

design.description: One design version. Coordinates in mm, ISO 8855 axes (x forward, y left, z up), origin on the ground below the middle of the front axle, so everything behind the front axle has negative x (the rear axle is at x = -wheelbase). Versions are never rewritten; a change makes a new version.

variables.description: Named design variables, e.g. wheelbase, track, cg_height.

modules.description: Present when the design's generator splits it into modules; then revise_design takes module and build_version makes versions.

module_changes.description: The proposals this version was built from (empty or absent for version 1 and for designs without modules).

archetype.description: The generator (hiraku.designgen ARCHETYPES name) that built this design; absent for a hand-made design.

variable_names.description: Design variable name -> its name for a person (Japanese), written by the generator; the screen shows these instead of the variable ids.

criterion.description: Pass condition of a load case. The limit is computed by code from requirements (and materials) when the load case is built.

basis.description: How the limit was made, e.g. 'yield 235 MPa / Q61 1.5'.

stand_in_quantity.description: A result quantity whose latest comparison stands in for the judged quantity's when both the prediction and the result of the judged quantity are below 1e-6 of the limit (e.g. stress_range for a fatigue_damage near zero). The verdict still uses the judged quantity.

params.description: Test conditions. params.loading (string) chooses who and what is on board: empty, driver, two, two_cargo (catalog Q30). Without it, solvers use two_cargo.

tolerance_rel.description: Allowed |analyzed - predicted| / |predicted| for a match. Set by code from the catalog or tool spec, never by the model.

feeds.description: Load cases that take this case's results as input (e.g. P1 wheel force feeds R1).

modules.description: The modules whose designers answer a red of this case (set by the builder; package when only the layout can fix it).

formula.description: A K0 hand-calculation formula as listed on the tool shelf.

term.description: One term of a formula or one effect, used for contribution and explanation.

share.description: Fraction of the total, or elasticity for sensitivities.

prediction.description: A hand-calculated prediction. The value is computed by K0 from formula_id and inputs, never typed by the model.

quantity.description: Name of the predicted quantity, e.g. front_wheel_force, max_stress.

tool_check.description: One known-answer case a tool must reproduce before it is usable.

tolerance_abs.description: Absolute tolerance, used where the expected value is 0 (or so small that tolerance_rel means nothing): |value - expected| <= tolerance_abs.

source.description: Where the expected value comes from (closed form, textbook, ...).

code_hash.description: Hash of the hiraku package's source the check ran on (every .py file). A check may be reused by a later run only while this hash is unchanged.

cached_from.description: When the check was not run again but reused: the run_id whose check is reused (same code_hash). Absent when the check ran in this run.

tool_spec.description: An analysis tool on the shelf (A4). A tool with usable=false must not be run.

formulas.description: K0 formula ids that predict this tool's quantities.

stage.description: How heavy the tool is, for the order of checks: 0 layout and rules (geometry, interference, occupants, system chains), 1 light (hand-calc sized models, beams, lumped thermal), 2 dynamics (vehicle time simulations), 3 heavy (shell and solid FE, convergence, fatigue on spectra, time-varying fields). Missing: 1.

applies_to.description: Kinds of design (hiraku.designgen ARCHETYPES keys) whose designs the tool can analyse. Missing: any design.

where.description: Member, node, support or part id where the value occurs.

field.description: A field to draw as a contour or mode shape.

kind.description: error_estimate: estimated discretisation error of the stress in each element (per_element, unit %), e.g. Zienkiewicz-Zhu: the energy norm of (recovered smooth stress - element stress) over that of the recovered stress. Shows where the mesh should be finer.

per_node.description: Per node value; for mode_shape a vec3 displacement relative to the largest (unitless shape, scaled by the screen).

mesh_id.description: With per_element / per_mesh_node: the mesh the values belong to.

per_element.description: One value per element of the mesh, in its element order.

per_mesh_node.description: One value per mesh node, in nodes_mm order (vec3 for displacement and mode shapes).

surface.description: For shell stresses: which surface of the wall (max = the larger of top and bottom).

frames.description: The same field at chosen moments of a time history (e.g. the frame stress solved at each kept step of a K2 run). Each list has one entry per t_s. The screen colours by the entry nearest to the replay time.

source_analysis_id.description: The analysis whose time history gave the loads.

per_element.description: With mesh_id: one per_element list per moment.

max.description: The largest value at each moment.

mesh.description: runs/<run_id>/v<NNN>/meshes/mesh-NNNN.json: a finite-element mesh made by code from one design version: shells on the mid-surfaces of tube walls and plates, solids for thick parts, or both with connections. Analyses of that version name it by mesh_id in their fields.

mesher.description: What made the mesh, e.g. frame_mesh (the version's shell mesh) or frame_tubes (one shell mesh per tube, tied). A version may have more than one mesh; each field names the one it is on by mesh_id.

element_type.description: shell: 3 or 4 nodes on the mid-surface; solid: hexahedra (8 or 20 nodes); mixed: both, with element_kind per element and the links in connections.

formulation.description: Element formulation in words, e.g. MITC4.

elements.description: Node indices (into nodes_mm). quad4 and tri3: counter-clockwise seen from the outer side. hex8: nodes 0-3 counter-clockwise seen from +zeta (the bottom face), 4-7 above them in the same order. hex20: the 8 corner nodes, then the mid-edge nodes of edges 0-1, 1-2, 2-3, 3-0, 4-5, 5-6, 6-7, 7-4, 0-4, 1-5, 2-6, 3-7.

element_kind.description: For each element, its kind. Required when element_type is mixed.

element_member.description: For each element, the design member (or part) id it belongs to.

member_thickness_mm.description: Wall thickness of each shell member (or part) in the mesh. Required when element_type is shell.

notes.description: How the joints, welds and load points were modelled.

quality.description: Mesh check made by code before the solve (pre-processing). Limits are the solver's stated rules of thumb (assumption unless a source is given in notes).

verdict.description: fail: the solver refuses the mesh; warn: solved, but the listed metrics are past their limits.

metrics.description: e.g. aspect_ratio, warp_deg, skew_deg, min_angle_deg, max_angle_deg, jacobian_ratio, taper.

per_element.description: Optional: one value per element for a metric, in element order (for drawing).

connections.description: Links between nodes that are not elements: rigid and interpolating ties, springs and bushes, shell-to-solid joints and tied faces.

kind.description: rbe2: rigid link from master to nodes; rbe3: master moves as the weighted average of nodes (adds no stiffness); spring: 6-dof spring or bush between two nodes; shell_solid: shell edge nodes tied to solid_nodes over thickness_mm; tie: faces glued to a surface that does not share nodes.

master.description: rbe2: the independent node; rbe3: the reference (dependent) node.

stiffness.description: spring: kx, ky, kz in N/mm and krx, kry, krz in N*mm/rad, along frame.

faces.description: tie: the faces (4 to 8 nodes) glued to the other surface.

vector.description: An arrow to draw: a reaction, grip force, applied load, wind, inertia, or the force the body receives at a suspension pickup (joint: at is '<support id>.<hardpoint key>').

origin_mm.description: Point where the force acts (application point), in the analysis's scene frame: design coordinates for a static analysis, the run's road frame (world axes, as scene and series) for a driving analysis.

series.description: Values against time (t_s) or against another quantity (x, e.g. wheel travel or lateral force on a K&C bench). Exactly one of t_s and x; its values have the same length as values.

analysis.description: One analysis run (RUN in the ER diagram). It cannot exist without at least one prediction.

inputs_from.description: Analysis or prediction ids whose values were used as inputs (e.g. the wheel force passed from P1 to R1).

timings_s.description: Clock times of parts of the analysis (name -> seconds, e.g. assembly, factorisation, convergence levels). They change from run to run: clock times go here or in wall_time_s only, never in results, effects, assumptions or text.

scene.description: What to draw around the vehicle for this test (from the load case and the solver, never hand-placed).

assumptions.description: Values the tool had to assume because neither the load case nor the design gives them (e.g. a default side-force coefficient).

setup.description: What the solver put on the model for this load case (pre-processing), for drawing and checking. Node numbers are indices into nodes_mm of the analysis's mesh (mesh_id).

spread_to.description: How a point load was distributed (RBE3-like): mesh nodes and weights.

inertia_relief.description: Unbalanced load taken by inertia instead of supports.

checks.description: Pre-processing checks: e.g. equilibrium_residual, model_mass, design_mass.

mesh_convergence.description: The judged value solved again on finer meshes of the same design (h-refinement), made by code. The meshes beyond the analysis's mesh_id are not recorded; levels gives their size and count.

quantity.description: Name of the result checked (as in results), e.g. hot-spot stress at a weld line.

mesh_id.description: When this level is the analysis's recorded mesh.

change_pct.description: |v_fine - v_next| / |v_fine| x 100 between the two finest levels.

extrapolated.description: Value at zero element size from three levels (Richardson extrapolation).

error_pct.description: Estimated error of the finest value against extrapolated, in %.

verdict.description: singular: the value keeps rising as the elements shrink (sharp corner, point load); it cannot be judged as it stands.

comparison.description: Prediction vs analysis. A mismatch blocks the domain until a cause is recorded.

diff_abs.description: analyzed - predicted, signed, in the unit of both.

diff_rel.description: (analyzed - predicted) / |predicted|, signed. status is match when |diff_rel| <= tolerance_rel.

where.description: Where the compared result is taken when a tool reports more than one place: a member or part id (e.g. rail_L_BE). Absent for a frame-wide or single result.

safe_side.description: The CAE role judged that the comparison, though a mismatch, is seen from the safe side: the cause explains the gap and the unfavourable one of the two values bounds the true value. Then a verdict may be made from that value.

safe_side_reason.description: Why the unfavourable value bounds the true one (required when safe_side is true).

ends_case.description: The mismatch cannot be settled for this load case in this run (no prediction the tools can check reaches the quantity, as the cause says): the load case ends not judged. HK4 does not wait for it and HK5 does not let it hold heavier stages; its tile stays not judged (never green). Not with safe_side.

verdict.description: Pass or fail of one test. Made inside the tools only: from a matching comparison (compare), from an explained safe-side mismatch (record_cause with safe_side true), or failing from an analysis whose results have unsupported_load > 0 (judge; the load has no path to the frame).

analysis_id.description: The analysis whose unsupported_load made this verdict (basis unsupported_load).

margin_pct.description: How far the value is from the limit, as % of the limit, positive when passing. null when the limit is 0 (use margin).

basis.description: match: from a matching comparison (value = analysis). explained_safe_side: from a mismatch whose cause has safe_side true and whose numbers confirm it (value = the unfavourable of prediction and analysis). Absent means match. unsupported_load: the analysis found load points with no path to the frame (value = their count, limit 0, pass false).

margin.description: How far the value is from the limit in its own unit, positive when passing.

judgement.description: Verdicts of one domain for one design version (one tile of A6).

test_ids.description: Optional: the tests of this domain that apply to the product's flags. The screen shows their count.

domains_picked.description: data of domains.picked: the lead's choice of domains for the product (screen A1). Emitted after run.started, before design.created.

flag_reasons.description: Why each flag was set (or left unset), in the lead's words.

off.description: Domains not picked and why. assembly is never listed here.

assembly_test_ids.description: Assembly and human tests (H, G) that apply. Not counted as a domain.

question.description: One question of hearing.asked: a requirement the run still needs.

ask.description: must: no value yet; confirm: a default is proposed for the person to accept or change.

allow_other.description: The person may write a value not in choices.

default.description: Used when no answer comes. basis says where the value is from ('not checked' when unchecked).

hearing_asked.description: data of hearing.asked: the missing requirements, asked once together (screen A2).

hearing_answered.description: data of hearing.answered: the answers (or defaults) as requirements. They are also in project.requirements.

rule_category.description: Knowledge rule category. Japanese names: sheet_metal 板金, fastener 締結, weld 溶接, tolerance 公差, human 人, battery 電池, assembly 組み立て, suspension サス, manufacturing 製造., system 系 (a product's needed systems are there and connected end to end)

rule_id.description: Knowledge rule id, e.g. SM-01, FS-02, U1-03.

rule.description: One knowledge rule: a design rule checked against the parts of a design.

doc_id.description: The knowledge_imported doc it came from.

text.description: The rule in words, as the person reads it.

kinds.description: Part kinds (part.kind) the rule is checked on.

check.description: Expression over a part's values (a boolean subset of Python), evaluated by code, never by the model.

origin.description: builtin: shipped with HIRAKU; dropped: from a file the person gave.

check_by.description: Who turned a sentence into check: a code pattern or Claude. Left out when the check came written with the rule (builtin rules, tables with expressions).

basis.description: Source of the rule; 'not checked' when unchecked.

knowledge_imported.description: data of knowledge.imported: one bundle of rules taken in (the builtin set, or a file the person dropped). Kept only in events; a dropped file itself may be kept in runs/<run_id>/knowledge/. Per doc_id the last knowledge.imported event wins (giving the same file again re-sends it, e.g. with more checks).

skipped.description: Lines of the file that did not become rules, and why.

rule_check.description: runs/<run_id>/v<NNN>/rule_checks/rchk-NNNN.json: one rule checked against the parts of one design version (screen A5). pass is true exactly when hits is empty; parts in not_evaluable were not checked.

targets.description: Ids of the parts the rule applied to. "design" stands for the whole design (e.g. a system rule that finds a part missing). Every part_id in hits and not_evaluable is among targets.

values.description: The part's values the check used.

not_evaluable.description: Parts the check could not be evaluated on, with the values the design lacks.

prop.description: The pet's prop: binder, pencil, spanner, steering_wheel, battery, windsock, crash_target, i_beam, tuning_fork, thermometer.

project.description: runs/<run_id>/project.json. Written at the start of a run; status and requirements are updated in place, everything else is append-only elsewhere.

driver.description: What drove the run: scripted (no Claude), agent_sdk (HIRAKU's own agent loop with the user's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), claude_code_plugin (the user's own Claude Code session with the HIRAKU plugin, under the user's own sign-in; HIRAKU does not call Claude).

cost_usd.description: API cost of the run so far; null where HIRAKU cannot know it (driver claude_code_plugin: the user's own Claude Code pays).

beyond.description: Tests that also get a load case beyond their limit (id ending -beyond, title starting 限界の外), for showing the failing side.

stop_after.description: Copied from the requirements file's stop_after when the run starts, so every process that opens the run reads it.

hearing.description: Who settles the missing requirement items. code (missing = code): start_run fills them from the file and defaults before the agents start. claude: start_run leaves them open and the lead asks the person with ask_user (wait_seconds). Copied to the project when the run starts.

event_kind.description: Closed list. Ask the lead (統括部) to add a kind; do not invent one locally.

event.description: One line of runs/<run_id>/events.jsonl. The screen draws only from these lines (live and replay). For *.recorded / *.created / analysis.finished / judgement.updated / tool.checked, data is the full record, identical to the record file.

seq.description: 0, 1, 2, ... with no gaps within a run.

t.description: Seconds since run.started; replay timing uses this.

text.description: Speech bubble or log line, shown as is.

stop_reason.description: Free text for people (may be English); the screen shows stop_code.

stop_code.description: Why the run ended, for the screen to word. done goes with status done, error with failed, the others with stopped.

tool_input.record_prediction.description: Agent-facing MCP tool. K0 evaluates formula_id with inputs; the model never supplies the value.

output.description: Which formula output is the predicted quantity, when the formula has more than one.

tool_input.analyze.description: Agent-facing MCP tool. One entry point for every analysis tool, so tools made during a run (N13) are callable without re-registering MCP tools.

result_quantity.description: Which analysis result to compare, when its name differs from the prediction's quantity.

ends_case.description: The mismatch cannot be settled for this load case in this run (no prediction the tools can check reaches the quantity, as the cause says): the load case ends not judged. HK4 does not wait for it and HK5 does not let it hold heavier stages; its tile stays not judged (never green). Not with safe_side.

assembly_step.description: One step of the assembly order (A7).

direction.description: Direction the part moves in when it goes in, e.g. -x, +z.

depends_on.description: Parts that must already be in place.

blocked_by.description: When it cannot go in: what blocks it.

to.description: What it is fastened to, e.g. 'node LS1', 'member rail_L_AS1', 'part susp_FL'.

kind.description: How it is fixed at that step: bushing and ball_joint are fixed with their own through-bolt or castle nut, so they need the same tool clearance as a bolt.

path_mm.description: Polyline the part's centre follows from outside the vehicle to its place (last point = its place).

text.description: The step in one Japanese sentence, built by code.

group_parts.description: When the step fits a group built beforehand (e.g. a suspension corner, part 'corner:FL'), the part ids in that group.

tool_blocked_by.description: Parts or members in the way of the hand and tool at this step (the step can still go in; blocked_by is for parts that stop it going in).

interference.description: Two things that overlap, at rest or somewhere in their motion.

condition.description: Where in the motion, e.g. 'steer 30 deg, bump 80 mm'.

tool_input.revise_design.description: Agent-facing MCP tool for the designer only. hiraku.designgen rebuilds the design from the changed variables and generator choices (changes, choices, or both); the store makes the next version with parent_version and change_reason.

changes.description: design variable name -> new value in the variable's own unit

reason.description: which test failed and what the change does about it

choices.description: generator choice name -> chosen value (as in propose_design.choices; the choices a design's generator offers are in get_context design_choices)

module.description: Required when the design has modules: the change is then a proposal for this module only (its variables and choices), recorded as design.change_proposed; build_version makes the version.

scene_object.description: Something in the test scene that is not the vehicle: a step, a road profile, a slope, the tilt table, a cone, a gate, a wall. Positions in mm in the road frame of the test (x along the road, z up), the vehicle starting at its design origin.

position_mm.description: Centre of the box (size_mm). A cone is a point; a gate is a line through it.

size_mm.description: Edge lengths of the box. A gate is [0, width, 0].

rpy_deg.description: Roll, pitch, yaw about the centre (roll + = left side up, pitch - = front up).

profile.description: Road height along x (road_profile), one line per wheel track when given.

angle_channel.description: Series channel that moves this object in time (e.g. table_angle for the tilt table).

report.description: The report (A8, N17). Numbers are filled by code from the records; the model writes only summary and next.

design_version.description: The version the report is about; 0 when the run stopped before version 1 (then the report carries only summary and issues).

line.description: One line of result for the domain.

effects.description: Terms that matter (from analysis effects and prediction terms).

unchecked.description: Values whose sources are not checked, picked up by code from requirements, materials and design.

rule_id.description: A rule_check hit this change answers; then domain may be one the run did not pick (e.g. assembly for a seat-depth rule).

tool_input.propose_design.description: Designer only: the first version from a design archetype; hiraku.designgen.kit computes every coordinate.

tool_input.write_report.description: Write the report: the model gives the summary and the next changes; numbers in them must match the records or the tool refuses.

rule_id.description: A rule_check hit this change answers; then domain may be one the run did not pick (e.g. assembly for a seat-depth rule).

issues.description: Optional: where HIRAKU itself was in the way during this run.

tool_input.make_tool.description: Agent-facing: write a tool (Python, the AnalysisTool shape with its own known-answer checks). It runs in a separate restricted process; it goes on this run's shelf only when every check passes. Every attempt is recorded with tool.checked (usable false when it fails).

reason.description: Which test needs it and why no tool on the shelf covers it.

tool_input.check_tool.description: Try a tool's own known-answer checks in the restricted process without putting it on the shelf.

tool_input.pick_domains.description: Agent-facing MCP tool (受付部, hiraku/intake/tools.py). 作りたいもの (文) から、使う解析の分野を選ぶ。まとめ役が使う。flags は文から読み取った製品の性質 (true の物だけでよい。理由は flag_reasons に 1 つずつ)。分野とその試験は、カタログの発動条件からコードが決める (あなたは決めない)。あなたが書くのは: 各分野を使う (使わない) 理由 reasons、製品に合わせた分野の呼び名 shown_names (たとえば配膳ロボの空力は「液体のこぼれ」)。理由が足りない分野はコードの仮の理由が付くので、結果の reasons_missing を見て付け足す。人が札を外したときは exclude。 製品の性質: - ride (乗): 人が乗って一緒に動くか - lean (預): 人が体を預けるか (寝る・座る・もたれる・手をつく) - self_propelled (走): 自分の動力で移動するか - outdoor (外): 屋外で使うか - rough (悪): 未舗装・凹凸の路面を走るか - public_road (公): 公道を走るか (法令の区分に入るか) - battery (池): 電池を積むか - electric (電): 電動で動く部分があるか (モーター・アクチュエータ) - pinch (挟): 動く部分に体が入る隙間があるか - cargo (荷): 物を載せるか - standing (置): 床・地面に自立して置くか (倒れうるか) - near_people (近): 人のすぐ近くを動くか - liquid (液): 液体を運ぶか - vibration (振): 振動源があるか (回転・弦) - continuous (続): 発熱が問題になるほど連続で動くか - assembly (組): 組み立て・分解・整備があるか - preload (張): 常にかかる内力があるか (弦・ばね) - sound (音): 音が機能か - handheld (持): 手で持つ・身に着けるか 速さの域 speed_class: - static (静): 動かない - walk (歩): 歩く速さ (2 m/s 以下) - vehicle (車): 車の速さ (40 km/h 以下)

want.description: 人が作りたいものを言った文、そのまま

flags.description: 製品の性質。立てるものだけ true で渡す

flag_reasons.description: フラグ → 立てた (立てなかった) 理由。A1 のチップの説明になる

reasons.description: 分野 → この製品でその分野を使う理由 (1 文)

shown_names.description: 分野 → 画面に出す呼び名 (読み替えるときだけ)

tool_input.ask_user.description: Agent-facing MCP tool (受付部, hiraku/intake/tools.py). 要件のうち、この製品に要るのに実行の要件に無いもの (必須・確認) を、まとめて 1 回聞く。質問と選択肢はコードが 項目の表から作る。答えが無い確認の質問は、出どころつきの既定値を使う。必須の質問は答えが無いと進めない。answers には、人が実際に言ったことだけを {要件の番号: 値 か {value, unit, basis}} で入れる (推測で埋めない)。answers_file は data/requirements/products/ の答えのファイル。質問を製品に合わせて言い換えたいときは wording ({番号: 文})、選択肢を変えたいときは choices。画面の人の答えを待ちたいときは wait_seconds (質問を画面に出し、答えが来るか時間が切れるまで待つ)。

answers.description: 人の答え。値か {value, unit?, trust?, basis?}

wait_seconds.description: 答えが無いとき、画面の人の答えを最大この秒数だけ待つ。0 (既定) なら待たず、確認の質問は既定値で進む

answers_file.description: 答えのファイル (data/requirements/products/ の中)

wording.description: 質問の言い換え {番号: 文}

choices.description: 選択肢の言い換え {番号: [{label, value, unit?}]}

rule_hits.description: Rule hits that need the person's decision (change the design or drop the rule); asked with the requirement questions.

tool_input.import_knowledge.description: Agent-facing MCP tool (受付部, hiraku/intake/tools.py). 人が渡したファイル (Markdown・CSV/TSV の表・テキスト) を読み、規則にする。text と filename で渡す (または実行のフォルダの knowledge/ の中の path)。「A は B 以上」のような文はコードが式にする。式にできなかった文は 結果の needs_formula に番号 (c3 など) つきで返る: それぞれ、1 つの部品について はい / いいえ で答える式 check (結果の facts の名前だけ。要件は req_Q15、設計の変数は var_<名前>) を書いて formulas={番号: {check, kinds?, category?}} に入れ、同じ filename と text でもう一度呼ぶ。規則にならない文は skip={番号: 理由}。式の計算はコードがする。kinds は対象の部品の種類 (battery, seat, body など。frame は骨組み、support は接地点)。

path.description: 実行のフォルダの knowledge/ の中のファイル

tool_input.rule_check.description: Agent-facing MCP tool (受付部, hiraku/intake/tools.py). ナレッジの規則 (最初から入っているものと、渡されたファイルのもの) を設計の部品に当てる。パッケージ役が使う。結果は、当たった (規則に合わない) 部品、式に要る値が設計に無くて判定できなかった規則、数。disable は使わない規則の番号。規則が増えたとき、設計を直したあとにもう一度呼ぶ。

design_version.description: 当てる設計の版 (無ければ最新)

issue.description: Where the run got stuck or had to work around HIRAKU itself (not a design result): input for improving HIRAKU.

what.description: What was missing or went wrong, in one or two sentences.

record_ids.description: Records that show it (ana-, pred-, cmp-, cause-, tool ids).

workaround.description: What the agent did instead, e.g. made a tool in the run, assumed a value.

rule_question.description: A rule hit the person must decide on: change the design, or drop the rule for this run.

text.description: The question in the person's words (the rule, what it hit, why it matters).

module_id.description: A design module (2026-11-04). package = レイアウト (wheelbase, track, rail spacing and height, where each module's space is; owned by the packager, no parts); frame = 枠 (rails, cross members, towers, posts, gussets, the frame's own brackets); suspension = 足まわり (wheels, knuckles, arms, dampers, their mounts on the frame); steering = 操作系 (steering wheel, column, shaft, rack, tie rods, pedals, pedal post, master cylinder); occupant = 乗員まわり (seats, belts, side guard, door or opening, grab bars, roll bar; the people are placed here); powertrain = 動力 (motor, reducer, driveshafts, battery, controller, aux, switch, wiring); body = 車体 (floor, deck, bulkhead, front body, fenders, cargo).

interface.description: Where two modules meet: the packager fixes it; module designers may not move it.

node.description: A frame node id, when the interface is at a node.

via.description: As connects_to.via: weld, bolt, bushing, ball_joint, pin, ...

module.description: One module of a design: who owns it, the space it may use and the variables and choices it may change.

envelope.description: Boxes of space this module's parts and members must stay inside (set by the packager; empty for package).

variables.description: Design variables this module's designer may change.

choices.description: Generator choices this module's designer may make.

module_change.description: One module designer's proposal for the next version (revise_design with module). build_version builds every pending proposal of the round into one version. The packager's own change of a round may be one more entry with module_id package and agent_id packager.

load_case_ids.description: The red load cases this change answers.

changes.description: design variable name -> new value in the variable's own unit

choices.description: generator choice name -> chosen value (as in propose_design.choices; the choices a design's generator offers are in get_context design_choices)

design_version.description: The version this proposal was made on (the red it answers is on that version).

tool_input.build_version.description: Agent-facing MCP tool for the packager only, for designs with modules: builds the next version from every pending module_change of the round plus the packager's own changes (package variables, envelopes, interfaces). Refused while two proposals change the same variable or a proposal's parts would leave its module's envelope.

changes.description: design variable name -> new value in the variable's own unit

regrow.description: Modules whose envelopes the code re-grows around their parts in the new version (designgen.modules.envelopes), instead of boxes written in envelopes. The packager names each module on purpose and says why in reason; overlaps between modules are still judged by H1-interference.

version_load_cases.description: The load cases built for one design version (a builder's criterion may read the version's own design, e.g. how many parts to assemble). Written to v00N/load_cases.json; project.load_cases stays the first version's.
